mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rebounded from -6.7 to 2.1 over the last two weeks, indicating restored commuting routines that bring workers past retail corridors, which will sustain higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining positive or rising for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops more than 2 points week-on-week after a multi-week rise, it signals households resuming out-of-home discretionary activity, which raises RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls more than 2 points week-on-week after at least two prior weeks of increase
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 (t-1w) to 6.4 (t-0w) after rising for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a RESIDENTIAL drop of more than 2 points that follows a multi-week rise.

mechanism_narrative: The t-1w dip across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES coincident with a RESIDENTIAL spike reflects a holiday-week pattern (e.g., July 4 week); post-holiday reversion will lift RETAIL_REC for two weeks before stabilizing.
candidate_trigger: a single-week synchronized dip in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES with a RESIDENTIAL spike, followed by partial rebound
evidence_refs: fact:all activity series dipped at t-1w while RESIDENTIAL peaked at 9.6, then partially reverted at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or continues declining for two weeks after the identified holiday-pattern dip instead of rebounding toward pre-dip levels.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (both rising from t-1w to t-0w) jointly signals resumed commuting that compounds with transit-adjacent shopping trips, producing a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -4.9 to 2.1 and TRANSIT rose from -16.0 to -9.0 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks is no larger than what a single-series (WORKPLACES-only) model predicts, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The rebound in PARKS from -45.3 to -36.4 alongside TRANSIT recovery suggests loosened local restrictions or removed capacity limits on public spaces, which will support continued RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks as restriction-sensitive behavior normalizes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT also rises
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 8.9 points and TRANSIT rose 7.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to trend upward over four weeks despite continued joint increases in PARKS and TRANSIT, implying the restriction-easing mechanism is not operative.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility stays persistently elevated above 10 points for two or more consecutive weeks, it indicates stable essential-trip activity that frees household budgets/time for discretionary retail, triggering a rise in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 10 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 11.0 at t-3w and 12.1 at t-0w, both above 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following two consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM above 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: An inverse co-movement between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES (RESIDENTIAL falling as WORKPLACES rises) signals a shift from home-bound to out-of-home routines; when this divergence exceeds 5 points combined, it amplifies near-term RETAIL_REC gains beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises in the same week with combined magnitude change exceeding 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 3.2 points and WORKPLACES rose 7.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC gain in the following week is equal to or smaller than the gain predicted by WORKPLACES alone, indicating no amplifying interaction with RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent deep negative PARKS readings (below -35) during mid-summer reflect heat-driven avoidance of outdoor recreation, which structurally redirects discretionary activity toward indoor retail and recreation venues, sustaining positive pressure on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has remained below -35 across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to trend upward over four weeks while PARKS remains persistently below -35, indicating no substitution effect from outdoor to indoor activity.
